title: All-Remote Work: Async, Handbook-First, Non-Linear Workday
content:
# All-Remote Work: Async, Handbook-First, Non-Linear Workday

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/ (and /handbook-first/, /asynchronous/, /non-linear-workday/)
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## What "all-remote" means at GitLab

GitLab is one of the world's largest **all-remote** companies. GitLab uses the term "all-remote" (not hybrid or distributed) to describe its 100% remote workforce across 65+ countries. There is no GitLab office — all team members work from wherever they are.

## Handbook-First Communication

GitLab is intentional about documenting in a manner that creates a **single source of truth**. The company operates **handbook-first**, and in valuing transparency, makes its handbook publicly accessible.

### Terminology

At GitLab, documentation is written **before** the change is communicated. You document the solution first, then announce via Slack or email. This way there is no post-change documentation step that gets skipped.

The goal is not "documentation for its own sake" — it's that **net new solutions are documented in a universally accessible handbook before dissemination**, and iterations are made to the single source of truth.

### Why handbook-first matters

- As a team scales, the need for documentation increases in parallel with the cost of not doing it.
- A handbook-first organization benefits from a single source of truth.
- Without structured documentation, teams re-ask the same questions and lose to interruptions and suboptimal knowledge transfers.

### Slack retention policy — a forcing function

**Only 90 days of Slack activity is retained.** After 90 days, it's gone. This is intentional — it prevents Slack from becoming a project-management tool and forces team members to document in the handbook.

Discussions begin in **GitLab Issues or Merge Requests**, not in Slack. This ensures that whatever is merged into the handbook has a proper trail.

Slack is for **informal communication** (chat, quick questions) only.

## Asynchronous Work

GitLab provides extensive guidance on embracing asynchronous communication. Async work allows team members across time zones to contribute effectively without requiring real-time presence.

### Core async practices

- Use GitLab Issues and Merge Requests for discussions, not meetings.
- Make meeting agendas and notes available async — ideally in a shared Google Doc linked from the calendar invite.
- Record synchronous meetings and share with the broader team.
- Live-document meetings: participants type into the shared doc during the meeting, contributing asynchronously and synchronously.
- Avoid calendar tetris. Favor writing over real-time meetings.

### Async benefits

- Enables a global workforce across time zones.
- Reduces meeting burden.
- Creates a written trail — perfect for compliance and onboarding.
- Supports deep work and mental health (less interruption).
- Bridges the knowledge gap — written history is searchable and distributable.

## Non-Linear Workday

GitLab supports a **non-linear workday** — the idea that remote workers may not work 9-to-5 in a single block, and that's fine as long as results are delivered.

- **Flexible working hours** mean you can step away when needed without guilt.
- Regular life activities — going to the gym, taking a nap, grocery shopping, helping loved ones — are part of normal work-life integration.
- No glorification of overwork. Not taking time off is viewed as a weakness, not a strength.
- GitLab measures **impact, not activity** (see the TeamOps framework at `/teamops/measurement-clarity/#measure-impact-not-activity`).

## Expectations for All-Remote Team Members

### Communication expectations

- **Write things down first.** Don't bury knowledge in 1:1 conversations or Slack DMs.
- **Handbook-first.** If a decision is made, update the handbook. If the handbook is wrong, fix it via MR.
- **Transparency by default.** Default to public channels (both within GitLab Slack and within the public handbook).
- **Notify early for PTO.** Give advance notice at least **2× as many days as the planned time off** (e.g., 6 business days for 3 days off).

### Time zone expectations

- Respect time zones in meeting scheduling — rotate meeting times so the pain is shared.
- Async-first: don't require synchronous attendance unless critical.
- Use tools like `worldtimebuddy.com` for scheduling across regions.

### On-call expectations

- On-call is coordinated and documented for the engineering on-call rotation (see `/handbook/engineering/on-call/`).
- Scheduled leave for on-call team members follows the coverage-handoff process documented in each oncall page.

## Remote Onboarding Expectations

- **Take at least 2 full weeks** for onboarding before starting team-specific work in week 3.
- Use the onboarding issue template as a self-service, self-driven learning flow.
- Dogfood GitLab — all onboarding tasks are completed in GitLab Issues.
- Early social connection is critical — join `#new_team_members` and introduce yourself on day 1.

## Key Principles

1. **Handbook-first** — document before announcing.
2. **Asynchronous by default** — meetings are the exception, not the rule.
3. **Single source of truth** — the handbook. If it's not in the handbook, it's not policy.
4. **Iteration** — handbooks are never finished.
5. **Transparency** — public by default.
6. **Results, not activity** — measure impact, not hours.
7. **Bias toward asynchronous communication** — give others time to process before expecting a response.

## Further Reading (subpages)

- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/handbook-first/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/asynchronous/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/non-linear-workday/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/building-culture/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/informal-communication/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/meetings/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/mental-health/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/working-while-traveling/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/onboarding/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/remote-benefits/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/workspace/`
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/the-gitlab-test-remote-work/` — 12-step framework for evaluating remote readiness
- `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/stages/` — 10 models of remote and hybrid work

title: Navan Purchasing Card Policy (Corporate Credit Card)
content:
# Navan Purchasing Card Policy (Corporate Credit Card)

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/accounts-payable/corp-credit-cards/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## 1. Policy

- The Navan Purchasing Card policy facilitates lower-cost purchases necessary for company operations.
- It does **not** override GitLab's Procurement Policy — it provides an alternative for lower-cost goods and services.
- Cards are used for appropriate business purposes with regular controls.

**This policy applies to:**
- Ad hoc vendors spending **less than $5,000 USD annually**.
- Transactions where the vendor only accepts credit card payments.

**The policy restricts card use:**
- Cards **cannot** be used to bypass the GitLab Procurement process.
- **No charges above $5,000 USD annually per vendor** — these must go through Zip for procurement processing.
- **No items already noted as non-permissible in the Expense policy (e.g., software)**.
- No items listed as "non-permissible" below.

Cards are only provided to team members under their own name, with the request/approval of the Direct Manager and the VP Accounting Operation's final approval. Cards/card numbers **must not be shared** among team members.

## 2. General Guidelines

- **All card charges require a receipt.** US team members require receipts only for anything **over $50**. Receipts must be uploaded into Navan within **30 days** of the transaction date.
- If a receipt is missing, a **Missing Receipt Affidavit** must be completed and attached (as a PDF) to the expense.
- Use the appropriate Expense type for proper allocation. If not listed, use "Other" with supporting details in the description.
- Add expense tags under "Classifications" where applicable (e.g. company-wide events, marketing campaigns, professional services).
- Non-Permissible items will be flagged upon charge.
- **Single transactions must not exceed $5,000 USD.** For any purchase over $5,000, enter a Purchase Requisition in Zip.
- If a charge is made in error, raise a HelpLab ticket with the Expense admin team. Avoid charges in error.

## 3. Permissible Items

### Team Building Activities / Off-Site / Event Costs

- Registration fees for team building and off-site events, dinners, deposits for activities, and room rentals (all **under $5,000 USD**).
- **Team meals of up to 20 people**, not to exceed **$100 per person**.

### Gifts for Significant Life Events

- **Up to $125 USD per gift** for significant life events.
- Managers may send gifts and flowers on behalf of team members (e.g., well wishes before surgery or for loss of a loved one). **Baby gifts are not reimbursable** (GitLab already sends them a gift).
- Executive Business Assistants may purchase gifts for team members on behalf of managers; an email or Slack pre-approval from the manager must be attached.
- **Gift cards for team members are not allowed** for these gifts.
- Expenses are tracked by department; the submitter must be in the same department as the recipient.

### Shipping & Postage Fees

- Shipping for event items, prizes, gifts for significant life events.
- SWAG shipping follows the merchandise workflow in the Marketing handbook.

## 4. Non-Permissible Items

Any purchase **over $5,000 USD** (or equivalent local currency) is not permissible. Items below must be expensed personally through normal reimbursement or procurement:

### Airfare and related costs
- Airfare for an individual team member must be purchased through Navan.
- Includes in-flight purchases, seat upgrades, wifi, baggage costs, and meals.
- Personal expenses follow the normal expense policy.

### Hotels, Transportation & Related Travel Expenses
- Not permitted for individual team members on the Navan Purchasing Card.
- Examples: meals, wifi, Global Entry / passport charges, car rental, mileage, Uber/Lyft for personal use.
- These must be expensed via the employee reimbursement process.

### Co-working Space
- Not permitted for individual team members — must run through the normal expense reimbursement process.
- Only permitted if the space is used for an event.

### Software
- **All software purchases are non-permissible** on the Navan Purchasing Card (see Individual Use Software policy — purchases must go through the virtual-card workflow after Security/Privacy review).

### Other non-permissible
- Personal items of any kind
- Fines, penalties, or legal fees not incurred as GitLab business
- Cash advances
- Any item or service deemed inappropriate for corporate spend

## Additional Thresholds Summary

| Category | Limit |
|---|---|
| Single transaction on Navan card | **$5,000 USD** |
| Annual spend on one vendor via Navan card | **$5,000 USD** |
| Team meal | **$100 per person**, up to 20 people |
| Gift for significant life event | **$125 USD** |
| Receipt required threshold (US) | **Over $50** |
| Receipt upload window | **30 days** from transaction |
| Missing receipt remedy | Missing Receipt Affidavit (PDF) |

title: Spending Company Money (Expenses & Reimbursement)
content:
# Spending Company Money (Expenses & Reimbursement)

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/spending-company-money/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

**All team members and contractors must protect our Company assets, such as equipment, supplies, cash, and information. Treat Company assets with the same care you would if they were your own. No team member or contractor may commit theft, fraud or embezzlement, or misuse Company property.**

## Guidelines

1. As a public company, GitLab has an obligation to act in the best interests of the corporation and its shareholders. This obligation is shared by all team members and is the basis of our global travel and expense policy; team members must be thoughtful in spending the Company's money.
2. Spending Company money includes travel and expenses.
3. You may privately use GitLab property, a MacBook for example, to check your private e-mails or watch a movie as long as it does not violate the law, harm GitLab, or interfere with Intellectual Property. More details are in the Internal Acceptable Use Policy (`/handbook/people-group/acceptable-use-policy`).
4. **File your expense report in a timely manner; expense claims over 90 days from purchase date will not be reimbursed unless approved by your Manager.** The sooner it is submitted, the sooner you will get reimbursement.
5. If team members knowingly submit expenses for reimbursement for personal purchases that are not covered in the expense policy, this is a violation of the GitLab Code of Business Conduct & Ethics.

## Policy Links and Resources

| Policy Name | Owner | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Global Travel and Expense Policy (`/handbook/finance/expenses/`) | CFO | Policy and procedures by which reimbursable expenses are reimbursed |
| Procurement Process (PO) (`/handbook/finance/procurement/`) | VP Finance | Process to engage the procurement team |
| Spending Company Money (`/handbook/finance/spending-company-money/`) | CFO | Policy on spending Company money; links to resources |
| Internal Acceptable Use Policy (`/handbook/people-group/acceptable-use-policy`) | CPO, CLO | Requirements related to the use of GitLab computing resources and data assets |
| Growth and Development Benefit (`/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/`) | CPO | Access external resources to develop careers |
| Navan Physical Card Policy (`/handbook/finance/accounts-payable/corp-credit-cards/`) | CFO | Guidelines for acceptable use of physical corporate cards |
| GitLab Related Party Transactions (`/handbook/legal/gitlab-related-party-transactions-policy/`) | CLO | Related Party Transactions Policy |

## Ways to spend company money

1. **Individual expenses on a personal credit card** — see the Global Travel and Expense Policy for what's reimbursable and how to submit.
2. **Individual expenses using a virtual card** — see the Global Travel and Expense Policy.
3. **Individual expenses using a Navan physical card** — see the Navan Physical Card Policy.
4. **Company expenses using a Coupa virtual card** — see the Coupa Virtual Card guide under Enterprise Applications.
5. **Company expenses using a purchase order** — see the Procurement Process.

## Expense tooling

- **Navan** is GitLab's expense tool used for personal expense reimbursement and for issuing virtual cards for approved one-time purchases.
- **Coupa** is used for purchase orders (POs) and vendor payments.
- **Zip** is the procurement intake tool where purchase requests are submitted, reviewed, and approved.

## Submission deadline

- Expense claims **over 90 days from the purchase date will not be reimbursed** without Manager approval.
- Receipts must be uploaded into Navan within **30 days of the transaction date** for corporate card usage.
- US team members using corporate cards need receipts for any single charge **over $50**; other jurisdictions require receipts for every charge.
- A Missing Receipt Affidavit (PDF) must be submitted if a receipt is lost.

## Notes on tax and reimbursement limits

- The Global Travel and Expense Policy (detailed limits, per-diem amounts, meal caps) now lives in the GitLab **internal handbook** at `https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/expenses/` and is only accessible to active GitLab team members.
- For home office and equipment expenses, see the Equipment section of the internal handbook's Expenses page, or submit via Navan. Questions go to `expenses@gitlab.com` or HelpLab.

title: Flexible PTO, Public Holidays, Sick Time, Bereavement, Jury Duty
content:
# Flexible PTO, Public Holidays, Sick Time, Bereavement, Jury Duty

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO)

### Overview

GitLab offers a Flexible PTO policy that empowers team members to take the time they need while ensuring business continuity.

- As long as you have coordinated with your manager about your planned time off and made a coverage plan, you are free to take PTO.
- **GitLab does not set a specific limit on the amount of PTO per year.** However, for time off exceeding **25 consecutive calendar days** (including weekends and holidays), special permission is required from your Manager, People Business Partner, and the Absence Management Team at `leaves@gitlab.com`.
- Team members **may not substitute PTO for sick time**. If taking time off for medical needs (physical or mental health), follow the Sick Time Policy.
- **GitLab strongly recommends taking at least two consecutive weeks of time off, and a minimum of 25 days total per year.**

### PTO Protocols

- Discuss planned time off with your manager first and provide as much notice as possible, but **at least twice as many days as your planned time off** (e.g., **6 business days notice for 3 days off**).
- Coordinate with your team and stakeholders, especially during popular holiday periods.
- If a manager needs to request changes to your PTO plans, they will do so within **48 hours** and specify the goal or result impacted. If no compromise can be reached, escalate to the manager's manager.

### How to Enter PTO in Workday

1. Enter PTO directly into the Workday app, or through the Workday Slack integration.
2. Select day(s) → Click "Time-Off" → Click "Paid Time Off" → (Optional: add a comment) → Click "Submit".

**All team members must log their time away in Workday.** Entries can be edited up to **30 days in the past**. Older entries require a HelpLab submission to the People Connect team.

### Absence without notification

**Absence for 72 hours without notification could be deemed job abandonment.**

## Public Holidays

- All team members will see a public holiday accrual balance in Workday.
- Balance is country-specific, determined by local / contractual requirements, and reviewed annually against benchmarked National Holidays data.
- **Balance must be used within the calendar year; unused public holiday balances will not rollover.**
- Team members **choose** which public holidays to observe (Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging principle).
- Public Holidays in Workday are 1-day entries — partial public holidays cannot be taken.
- **Contractors of GitLab GSI** receive a standardized allocation of **12 public holidays** (the weighted average across GitLab countries).

### Mid-year hire pro-ration

(Days remaining in the calendar year ÷ 365) × Full-year public holiday entitlement, rounded to the nearest whole day (up if decimal ≥ .5, down if < .5).

Example: If the country entitlement is 10 days and you joined with 92 days remaining, balance = 10 × (92 ÷ 365) = 2.52 → **3 days**.

## Sick Time

- Covers personal illness (e.g., COVID-19, cold/flu, menstrual pain, surgery) and preventative care.
- For caring for a sick family member, use the **Caregiver Sick Time** policy.
- GitLab's Sick Time runs **concurrently** with any statutory sick leave.
- **Each team member may use up to 25 paid sick days** in a **rolling 12-month period**, available from first day of work.
- **Pay:** 100% of weekly wages for up to 25 working days. If a statutory benefit is available, you must apply for it; GitLab supplements to reach 100% of wages. Beyond 25 working days, leave is unpaid (subject to local requirements).
- Sick time is not paid out upon termination (except where required by local law).

### Reporting Procedures

**1–5 consecutive days:**
1. Notify manager.
2. Enter the time in Workday, label **"Out Sick"**.
3. Time auto-syncs to Time Off by Deel.
4. **No sick note required** for less than 6 consecutive days (unless local statute requires).

**6+ consecutive days** (considered a leave of absence):
- **USA:** Submit to **Tilt** (accessed via Okta). Personalized leave plan is built within **2–5 business days**.
- **All other locations:** Notify the Absence Management team via HelpLab, enter time in Workday as "Out Sick", provide evidence per local requirements.

## Caregiver Sick Time

- For time away to care for ill family member: parent(s), child(ren), spouse, domestic partner, grandparent(s), grandchild(ren), or sibling(s).
- **Up to 25 paid caregiver sick days** per rolling 12-month period, available from first day.
- Runs concurrently with statutory family-care leave.
- Pay mirrors Sick Time: 100% of wages (with statutory supplement) up to 25 working days.
- 1–5 days: notify manager and enter in Workday labeled **"Caregiver Sick Time"**.
- 6+ days: considered a leave of absence (Tilt for USA; HelpLab for others), documentation required.

## Bereavement

Bereavement falls under the Flexible PTO framework. Available from day one.

- **No set limit on bereavement days.** Continuous or intermittent.
- **Inclusive:** not restricted by relationship to the deceased — includes loss of pregnancy (birthing and non-birthing parents), family, friends, colleagues, and **pets**.
- **No documentation required** unless local/statutory law requires it.
- **Compensation:** 100% of weekly wages; health insurance continues on the same terms.
- **If bereavement exceeds 25 calendar days:** contact Manager, People Business Partner, and `leaves@gitlab.com`.

Request process: notify your manager, enter in Workday → "Time-Off" → "Bereavement", create a coverage plan. Support resources include **Modern Health**, **Bereave** benefits, and EAP.

## Volunteer Time

Volunteer time falls under Flexible PTO. Manager coordination with 2× notice, then enter in Workday under "Time-Off" → "Volunteer". GiveLab is GitLab's Team Member Volunteer Program.

## Legal Civic Obligations (Jury Duty / Witness)

GitLab provides leave for any team member summoned to judicial, administrative, or quasi-judicial proceedings (jury duty, witness).

- Available from day one.
- **Up to 25 full working days of paid leave** per authorized leave (unless local law provides otherwise).
- **Pay:** 100% of weekly wages. If absence exceeds 25 working days, Absence Management reviews case-by-case.
- Enter in Workday → "Time-Off" → "Jury Duty" and attach a copy of the summons (or email `leaves@gitlab.com`).
- Runs concurrently with other job-protected / income-replacement leave as required by law.

## Workday: Single Source of Truth for Absence

- **All team members and managers must log time-away requests in Workday.**
- Workday syncs to Time Off by Deel, which syncs to Slack (OOO + Do Not Disturb) and Google Calendar.
- Time Off by Deel does **not** sync with GitLab.com — for absences over 48 hours, update your GitLab.com status manually (profile picture → Edit Status, e.g. "OOO Back on 2025-04-28").
- Managers with delegated approvals should set up a delegate in Workday for prolonged absences.
- Questions: HelpLab portal.

title: General Onboarding (New Hire Checklist)
content:
# General Onboarding (New Hire Checklist)

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/general-onboarding/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## Overview

Onboarding is incredibly important at GitLab. We don't expect you to hit the ground running from day one.

**We highly recommend taking at least two full weeks for onboarding and only in week three starting with team-specific onboarding and training.** Feel free to participate in your team's work in your first two weeks, but don't feel you have to contribute heavily.

All onboarding steps are in the onboarding issue template owned by the People Operations team (see `gitlab-com/people-group/people-operations/employment-templates`). The onboarding process for the new team member is self-driven, self-learning, and as asynchronous as possible to help settle into the remote life at GitLab.

At GitLab we dogfood our own product — all onboarding tasks are completed in a GitLab issue.

## Timeline

- **At least 4 days prior to hire date:** The People Operations Specialist assigned to the team member opens the onboarding issue.
- **Day 2 of onboarding:** An Access Request is generated (if a template exists for the role). Access requests are owned by the IT team. Questions to `#it-help` in Slack.
- **Main section due date:** 30 days.
- **Employment bot automatically closes** any onboarding issues still open after **60 days**.

In certain instances (national holiday, Family and Friends Day), People Operations may not be able to assist with onboardings. These dates are documented in the People Operations team availability.

## TaNewKi Welcome Call

The People Operations team hosts a **pre-onboarding call** (the "Ta-New-Ki" call — a play on Tanuki, the Japanese raccoon dog in our logo). The purpose is to give onboarding team members a chance to meet, socialize, and ask questions **before** their start date. Internally this is referred to as an AMA call.

- Hiring managers and current team members (e.g., onboarding buddies) are welcome to join.
- Occurs every two weeks on Thursday at three time slots to accommodate timezones:
  - **4:00 PM PT**
  - **12:00 AM PT**
  - **8:30 AM PT**
- Takes place **a week or two before actual start date**.

Agenda: review onboarding process on Day 1, encourage taking time, self-driven / self-service emphasis, Q&A.

## Slack Channels (All New Team Members Auto-Added)

By default, all new team members are added to these Slack channels from day 1:

- `#new_team_members` — go introduce yourself
- `#diversity_inclusion_and_belonging`
- `#it_help` — IT support (laptop, 1Password, Okta, JAMF, etc.)
- `#questions` — anything the Handbook can't answer
- `#donut-be-strangers` — coffee chat setup
- `#team-member-updates` — new team members, anniversaries, goodbyes
- `#thanks` — recognition/thanks
- `#whats-happening-at-gitlab` — company updates and notifications

## Managers of New Team Members

- Issue is created at least **4 business days prior to start date**.
- Manager and People Operations Team member are assigned.
- Both have tasks that need to be completed **prior to start date** for a smooth onboarding.

### Compliance

The Senior People Operations Specialist runs a **monthly audit** of all open onboarding issues to ensure the new team member, manager, and People Ops tasks are completed — especially tasks tied to company compliance (security, payroll, etc.). Outstanding tasks trigger a ping. The employment bot closes any issue open after **60 days**.

### Completing the Onboarding Issue

To ensure successful completion, all tasks must be checked off. Checking a box indicates one of:
- I have completed this task
- I have checked and this task is not applicable to me

## Onboarding Issue Templates

Public templates in `gitlab-com/people-group/people-operations/employment-templates`:
- **All GitLab team-members** (main template)
- **Intern** (dedicated template)

Role-specific country/role onboarding templates are in the same repo under `.gitlab/issue_templates/onboarding_tasks`.

### Supplemental onboarding issue templates

- Interviewing training issue
- Analytics group onboarding issue
- Becoming a GitLab manager issue
- Production engineering onboarding issue
- Security products technical onboarding issue
- Support engineer onboarding issue

## Related Onboarding Pages

- Developer onboarding (`/handbook/engineering/workflow/developer-onboarding/`)
- GitLab onboarding buddies (`/handbook/people-group/general-onboarding/onboarding-buddies`)
- Merge Request buddies (`/handbook/people-group/general-onboarding/mr-buddies`)
- Developer Experience Onboarding
- Sales team onboarding
- Support team onboarding
- SRE Onboarding
- UX Researcher onboarding

## Temporary Service Provider (Contractor / Consultant) Onboarding

The People team is **not involved** in hiring, onboarding, or offboarding of temporary service providers. Work with the Procurement team; the Temporary Service Provider internal handbook page has templates and helpful information.

## Buddy System

The **Onboarding Buddy** program pairs each new hire with an existing team member to provide social support, answer newbie questions, and help ease the onboarding experience. A Merge Request Buddy separately helps with code/MR review culture. Reach out to your onboarding buddy or to other GitLab team members for help with any onboarding tasks.

## Access Provisioning

Through onboarding issues, new team members gain access to baseline entitlements. **On Day 2**, an Access Request is generated if a template exists for the role. Access requests are owned by the IT team. Direct any questions to `#it-help` in Slack.

## Remote-specific Onboarding Guidance

GitLab recommends the onboarding process take **at least two full weeks**, with the third week designated for team-specific onboarding and training. Onboarding has three dimensions: organizational (logistics, tools, handbook), technical (using tools, early wins), and social (onboarding buddy, Slack intros, coffee chats).

Source references: `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/onboarding/`, `/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/getting-started/`.

title: Individual Use Software Purchases
content:
# Individual Use Software Purchases

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/procurement/individual-use-software/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## Individual Use Software Overview

Individual Use Software is software essential for executing job responsibilities and that is distinct from existing tools and platforms already owned or accessible to your team.

- An individual's **annual expenditure on Individual Use software must not surpass $5,000**.
- If the cost exceeds this threshold, or if multiple people on your team need access, follow the full Procurement process for a new purchase request.
- **All software purchases charged to either personal or corporate credit cards will be DENIED for reimbursement.** You must follow the Individual Use Software process. Approved purchases are paid via a Navan virtual card once all approvals are obtained.

Refer to the Internal Acceptable Use Policy (`/handbook/people-group/acceptable-use-policy/`) for questions regarding freeware, or to GitLab's Mobile Device Policy for information on accessing GitLab resources via Okta on a mobile device.

## I Need Individual Use Software — Where Do I Start?

First check the list of **Tech Stack applications** (`https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/www-gitlab-com/-/blob/master/data/tech_stack.yml`) and the **Pre-Approved Individual Use Software listing** in the internal handbook.

- **If your vendor is listed in the tech stack:** Submit an access request using the Individual Bulk Access Request template at `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/team-member-epics/access-requests`.
- **If your vendor is not in the tech stack:** Submit via the Individual Use Software Google Form (linked in the public handbook page) for appropriate routing.
  - Commonly requested software on the Pre-Approved Individual Use Software and Freeware list is subject to **expedited Security approval**.

Before pursuing a new vendor, consider whether one of our existing vendors can service your needs. Adding users to already-approved vendors:
- Saves GitLab money
- Decreases GitLab's threat landscape
- Expedites access

## What Happens When I Request Individual Use Software?

1. The Procurement team opens a GitLab Issue based on your responses and routes for necessary approvals, including your manager, Security, and Privacy.
2. Attach any relevant contracts, backups, or documents to the issue.
3. **Reviews may take several weeks**, depending on risk level, depth of review, and vendor responsiveness.
4. Once approved, the Procurement team issues you a **virtual one-time-use credit card via email** to purchase the approved software license at the approved price.
5. After purchase, forward a copy of your receipt to `ap@gitlab.com` if there are no other contracts or backup documents.

## Related Limits and Tools

- Cap: **$5,000 USD / year** per individual
- Physical Corporate Card (Navan) limit: **$5,000 USD** per transaction; annual $5k cap applies to the same Individual Use software rules (software purchases on the Navan Purchasing Card are explicitly **non-permissible**)
- Key tools: Okta, Zip (for over-cap requests), Navan (virtual card issued), HelpLab
- Slack channel: `#Procurement`

title: Parental Leave, Emergency Leave, Military Leave, Equity Vesting During Leave
content:
# Parental Leave, Emergency Leave, Military Leave, Equity Vesting During Leave

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/leave-types/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## GitLab Parental Leave

GitLab's paid Parental Leave is available for any active team member **regardless of gender** who becomes a parent through childbirth or adoption while working at GitLab. Different countries or US states may provide team members with their own statutory Parental Leave benefits.

### Eligibility, Entitlement, Planning

- **Available from your first day of employment**, provided your child was born or newly adopted during your employment at GitLab.
- **16 weeks of paid Parental Leave**, which must be used prior to the child's **first birthday or the first anniversary of adoption**.
- Leave may be taken all at once or split into **up to three segments**.
- **Calculation formula:** 1 week = 7 days. If you return on a Monday, your leave ends on Sunday.
- **If your Parental Leave falls within the 4 scheduled Family and Friends Days, parental leave is extended by 4 days.**
- Unused public holidays will not rollover to the next calendar year while on parental leave (unless statutorily required).

### No Work Required During Your Leave

- You are **not required** to log into any GitLab systems, review or approve compensation documents, or respond to any work-related emails or deadlines.
- Disregard automated system emails during leave; approvals are handled by the team or upon your return.
- Any compensation components will be preserved and addressed appropriately upon your return.

### Supplement with Paid Time Off

After Parental Leave, you may use Flexible PTO with manager coordination (following the 2× notice rule). Submit PTO in Workday under "Paid Time Off" and notify Absence Management.

**You cannot extend paid parental leave using Paid Caregiver Sick Time unless the family member has a serious health condition.**

### How to Initiate Your Leave

- **Share when comfortable.** Recommend communicating **2–3 months before** leave starts for workload planning.
- **30–45 days prior to leave**, submit your request per your location:
  - **USA and Canada:** Submit to **Tilt** (accessed through Okta). Personalized leave plan is built within **2–5 business days**. Contact: `LeaveSupport@ourtilt.com` or text **(970) 449-0178**.
  - **All other locations:** Enter Parental Leave in Workday under the Leaves dropdown → "GitLab Parental Leave". Absence Management will email within **48 hours**.
- **You cannot edit dates yourself** after approval — contact Absence Management for changes.
- Provide **proof of birth / relationship and/or adoption within 15 calendar days** from leave start. Email docs to `leaves@gitlab.com`.

### Pay While on Parental Leave

- **100% of weekly wages** through the GitLab Paid Parental Leave program.
- Where statutory leave pay is available in your country or US state, you are **required** to apply for it; GitLab supplements to equal 100% of wages.
- You will not receive more than 100% of your wages combined.

### Returning to Work

- About a week before your return, Absence Management sends a welcome-back email asking you to confirm your return date.
- **Returning at 50% capacity is available** — standard guideline is **2–4 weeks at reduced capacity**, flexible. Options:
  - Adjusting workload to ramp up gradually
  - Adjusting working days/hours (4×10 days, early/late shifts, etc.)
  - Gradually increasing working days (2 days week 1, 3 days week 2, etc.)
- This is NOT tracked in Workday and does not require Absence Management review.

## Emergency Leave

Emergency leave provides paid time away from work to use in unexpected scenarios such as natural disasters, community emergencies, or any other catastrophe. Available from **first day of work**.

### Request Process

1. Notify your manager as soon as possible (share only what you're comfortable with). You can also email `leaves@gitlab.com`.
2. Document in Workday: "Leaves" → "Emergency Leave" → Submit.
3. Absence Management contacts you within **48 hours** to confirm dates.

See also the People Group Incident Response Plan for what the People Group does when team members are impacted by an emergency event.

## Military Leave

GitLab protects the rights of team members absent for military leave. No discrimination or retaliation on the basis of uniformed-service membership.

- **Leaves ≤ 31 days:** No changes to job, pay, or benefits. Team member returns on next scheduled shift.
- **Leaves > 31 days:** Up to **6 months unpaid leave** (subject to statutory entitlement and business needs). Beyond 6 months the member is offboarded but eligible for reinstatement.
- **Healthcare:** May retain for up to **2 years or end of service** (whichever first), at own expense. Otherwise benefits end on **day 31**.
- **Stock vesting** continues up to 6 months of unpaid military leave.

**Reinstatement:** Up to **2 years** after service ends (2 years for disabilities). Required: proper notice, honorable release, and application within:
- **< 31 days:** report on next regularly scheduled work period
- **31–180 days:** apply within **14 days**
- **> 180 days:** apply within **90 days**

The "escalator principle" applies — the team member returns to the position they would have attained if they had not been called to serve.

**Applying:** Provide **30 days advance notice** via Workday → Leaves → "Military Leave". Documentation may be requested.

## Sick Leave

Sick absences **6 days or longer** are considered a leave of absence. See the Sick Time policy in the Time Off Types handbook page.

## Caregiving Sick Leave

Caregiver sick absences **6 days or longer** are considered a leave of absence.

## Equity Vesting During Leave

- Stock vesting is **paused after six months of continuous leave** and resumes on your first day back at work.
- Applied in accordance with applicable local laws and statutory requirements; may not apply in all locations or leave types.
- For details, see the Equity policy page. Questions to the Stock Admin team via HelpLab.

## Summary of Key Numbers

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Parental Leave duration | **16 weeks paid** |
| Parental Leave segments | Up to **3** |
| Must be used by | Child's 1st birthday / 1-year anniversary of adoption |
| Family & Friends Day bonus | **+4 days** if overlap |
| Proof of birth submission | **Within 15 calendar days** from leave start |
| Tilt leave-plan turnaround (USA/CA) | **2–5 business days** |
| Return at 50% capacity typical duration | **2–4 weeks** |
| Pay during parental leave | **100% of weekly wages** |
| Emergency Leave acknowledgement | Within **48 hours** |
| Military Leave max unpaid duration | **6 months** (up to) |
| Reinstatement window (>180 day service) | **90 days** from service end |
| Equity vesting pause threshold | **6 months** of continuous leave |

title: Procurement & Vendor Management
content:
# Procurement & Vendor Management

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/procurement/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## What is Procurement?

The Procurement team manages GitLab's Supplier Lifecycle through strategically vetting and selecting vendors, negotiating commercial terms, purchasing goods and services, and managing renewals or vendor offboarding.

## Procurement Team Alignment

Division alignment for spend over **>$25k USD / year**:

- Marketing — Ashley Abbate
- Sales — Ashley Abbate
- Product — Adrienne Ruhaak
- Engineering — Adrienne Ruhaak
- People — Adrienne Ruhaak
- Finance — Adrienne Ruhaak
- Legal — Adrienne Ruhaak
- All division spend **<$25k USD** — Dasha Yarmusik
- Individual Software Purchases — Anam Shaikh

## Vendor Lifecycle Management

1. **RFP and Vendor Selection** — All new spend, changing of vendors for existing services, and market reviews every 3 years must follow the RFP process. An NDA must be in place before sharing confidential information with potential vendors.
2. **Negotiation, Privacy, Security, and Compliance Review** — Depending on spend and data types, Procurement, Privacy, Security, and Ethics & Compliance review the vendor.
3. **Contracting** — Work must not begin until a contract is in place. See the Authorization Matrix for signing authority.
4. **Vendor Onboarding** — Vendors must complete onboarding in Coupa to be paid.
5. **Recurring Vendor Reviews and Management** — Quarterly Procurement & Business Spotlights review upcoming renewals, cancellations, and new spend.
6. **Cancellation** — Terminations/non-renewals go through Zip with Procurement and Legal coordination.

## The Procurement Process

Procurement must be engaged **BEFORE** a purchase or work begins (unless the spend qualifies as a personal expense or meets a documented exception).

Start the Procurement Process:
1. Before agreeing to any business, legal, or pricing terms with a supplier.
2. Immediately upon receiving a contract or quote for new or recurring business.
3. When evaluating a group of suppliers or starting an RFP.

### How to start — via Zip

The majority of the procurement process lives inside **Zip**, accessed via the Okta home page (`https://gitlab.okta.com/app/UserHome#`). Submit a Zip Request for:

- Purchase Requests for renewals of existing vendors' services
- Purchase Requests for new spend **under $25k**
- Change Requests to existing POs
- $0 contract reviews including demos and trials
- Partner Revenue Payments
- Individual Use Software requests
- Termination / Non-Renewal Notices

### RFP thresholds (new spend or vendor change)

| Annual spend | RFP type |
|---|---|
| Over $250K | Procurement-led RFP, typically **5+ vendor bids** |
| $100K – $250K | Business-led RFP, **2–3 vendor bids** required |
| $25K – $100K | Business-led quick-bid, **2 vendor bids** required |
| Under $25K | **No bid required** |

## Contingent Workers

The Contingent Worker Policy covers three categories: Staff Augmentation Workers (agency-provided temporary resources), Consultancy Services (third-party professional services), and Independent Contractors (used by exception only). The policy sets duration limits, country hiring guidelines, contractor extension processes, and background screening requirements.

For subcontractors for the Professional Services team, use the process for Revenue Partner Payments.

## Review Timelines

Requests can take **5 days to 3+ weeks** depending on factors including new vs. existing vendor, need for negotiation, data-sharing requiring Privacy/Security review, contract complexity, and vendor responsiveness.

### 1. Sanctions Screening (Ethics & Compliance): 30 minutes – 3+ days

- Uses Risk Rate tool automatically. Use the vendor's complete legal name.
- If Risk Rate detects a potential match or the vendor is in a high-risk country, it may escalate to Trade Compliance Counsel for manual review.
- Include the vendor's website or LinkedIn page in the Zip request.

### 2.A. Buyer Review (Procurement): 2 days

- Ensure contract documents are uploaded.
- The request dollar amount must match the contract value; correct billing codes must be selected.

### 2.B. New Supplier Onboarding: 2–3+ days

- Depends on supplier response time. After Procurement sets the vendor up in Coupa, the supplier receives an email requesting banking and tax information.
- Procurement **cannot** complete this on the supplier's behalf (SOX compliance).

### 3.A. FP&A Review: 2 days

- FP&A ensures the spend is within budget and the Billing Code is correct.

### 3.B. IT Review: 2 days (for new software or contractors)

- Requester should have the vendor complete the **IT New Software Questionnaire** for IT review.

### 4.A. Legal Review: 3 to 21 days

- **Existing vendors (renewals/upsells):** 3–5 days. Upload complete contract terms or link to the existing agreement.
- **New vendors:** 1–3+ weeks.
- Delays from vendor counsel extend the timeline.

## Key Tools

- **Zip** — Procurement intake system, accessed via Okta (`https://gitlab.okta.com/app/UserHome#`).
- **Coupa** — Invoicing and supplier-onboarding system (supplies banking/tax info).
- **Risk Rate** — Automated sanctions screening.
- **HelpLab** — Central request system for questions and access.
- **Slack:** `#procurement` for questions; tag `@procurement_team`.

## Exceptions to the PO Policy

If you have a **personal expense** or a purchase that meets documented PO exceptions, you do not need to engage Procurement. Otherwise, Procurement engagement is required.

## Escalation / Urgent Requests

If a request cannot meet the stated timelines and has specific and quantifiable business impact, follow the urgent-request steps (documented internally). Procurement and Legal will prioritize with justification.

title: Total Rewards: Compensation, Bonuses, Equity
content:
# Total Rewards: Compensation, Bonuses, Equity

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/compensation/ and https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## Compensation Philosophy

GitLab's compensation philosophy is to attract and reward team members who deliver meaningful results through collaboration while operating with efficiency as GitLab grows.

The standardized framework uses local labor market data to ensure fair and competitive compensation with a focus on transparency. It aligns compensation with pay for performance — through individual excellence and collaborative efforts.

## Compensation Elements

Total compensation at GitLab combines three components:

### 1. Base Salary

Base salary is annual guaranteed pay, typically paid in local currency. It's determined by **role, level, and location**.

GitLab sets base salary ranges using market data from compensation surveys (e.g., **Radford**), targeting compensation at or above the **50th percentile of the software industry**.

### 2. Variable Pay

Some roles include variable pay in addition to base salary. Variable pay has a target amount but is not guaranteed.

#### Director+ Bonuses

Directors and above (excluding those on a sales commission plan) have a bonus target that's a **percentage of base salary** and **paid twice per year (semi-annually)** based on company performance.

- Example: 15% of a $100,000 base salary = **$15,000 annual bonus target**.

#### Sales Commissions

Sales roles are structured as **On-Target Earnings (OTE)** = base salary + commission target. The split varies by role. Commission is tied to **quota achievement**:
- Hitting quota → full target commission
- Exceeding quota → upside
- Missing quota → lower commission

- Example: $100,000 OTE with a 60/40 split = **$60,000 base + $40,000 commission target**.

**Total Target Cash (TTC)** = base + variable target. For sales roles, often called OTE. TTC/OTE is what a team member would receive if **100% of targets are met**.

### 3. Equity (RSUs)

Equity compensation provides ownership in GitLab's future success through **Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)**. Shares vest over time. RSU value is tied to GitLab's stock price at sale.

Equity grants are given at:
- **New hire grants** as part of offer packages
- **Refresh grants** through Annual Compensation Review (performance + growth potential)
- **Promotion grants** when advancing to a new level

## When Compensation is Determined

### Time of Hire

Initial compensation package is determined when you join. Offers are based on:
- Market range for the role and level
- Location of the role
- Experience and skills as they relate to the role

### Annual Compensation Review (ACR)

- Company-wide review of all team member compensation, once per year.
- **Effective Date: May 1**
- Addresses market changes, recognizes performance, ensures internal equity.

## Equity: RSU Details

Since September 2021, GitLab has issued **Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)** for grants. GitLab is **no longer giving stock option grants**.

- RSUs are subject to forfeiture and are expected to **vest over 2–4 years** on a combination of **bi-annual and quarterly** basis.
- Governed by the 2021 Equity Incentive Plan.

### Sell-to-Cover (RSUs)

Shares are sold to pay taxes due on RSU vesting. Automatic sale based on your country's tax rate.

Example: if 100 shares vest and tax rate is 30%, 30 shares are sold to cover tax; 70 shares land in your E*TRADE account.

For US team members, withholding at vest uses federal supplemental tax rate + state/local + FICA + Social Security.

### Departure / Termination

If a team member leaves GitLab:
- **90 days post-termination to exercise any vested options.**
- **Unvested RSUs and options are forfeited** upon exit date.

## Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

The 2021 ESPP enables eligible team members to purchase Class A common stock via payroll deductions with:
- **15% purchase price discount** of fair market value on the IPO date or purchase date, whichever is lower.
- **24-month look-back** with **four purchase dates**: **May and November** of each year.
- First purchase occurred May 2022.

### Eligibility

1. Employed via a GitLab entity with **50+ headcount**.
2. Works more than **20 hours per week**.
3. Actively employed at the beginning of the Offering Period to enroll.
4. Actively employed on the last date of the Purchase Period to purchase.

Eligible ESPP GitLab entities include:
- GitLab Canada Corp.
- GitLab GmbH (Germany)
- GitLab B.V. (Netherlands/Belgium/Finland)
- GitLab Inc. (US)
- GitLab Federal, LLC
- GitLab UK Limited
- GitLab Pty Ltd (Australia/New Zealand)
- GitLab Ireland Limited
- GitLab France S.A.S. (from 2025-06-01)
- GitLab GK (Japan) (from 2025-12-01)
- GitLab India Private Limited (from 2025-12-01)

### Contribution Changes

- **Increases are NOT allowed** during Offering Period.
- **Decreases**: allowed once during any Offering Period.
- Team members may reduce contribution to **0%** during an offering period; prior contributions still purchase shares on scheduled purchase date.

## Referral Bonuses

GitLab has a referral program — see `/handbook/hiring/referral-process/` and `/handbook/total-rewards/incentives/#referral-bonuses` for eligibility and bonus amounts.

## Contact Total Rewards

- **Via HelpLab** — People Operations can direct questions to the right team.
- Slack: reach out to Total Rewards per `/handbook/people-group/#how-to-reach-the-right-member-of-the-people-group`.

## Summary of Key Numbers

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Target salary percentile | **50th of software industry** (per Radford survey) |
| Director+ bonus cadence | **Semi-annual** |
| Annual Compensation Review effective date | **May 1** |
| RSU vesting period | **2–4 years** (bi-annual + quarterly) |
| Post-termination option exercise window | **90 days** |
| ESPP discount | **15%** off FMV, 24-month lookback |
| ESPP purchase dates | **May and November** |
| ESPP min hours/week | **20+ hours** |
| ESPP min entity headcount | **50+** |

title: Travel Safety, Security, and Insurance
content:
# Travel Safety, Security, and Insurance

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/travel/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## Travel Safety and Security

Team member safety and security are a top priority for GitLab. If a team member feels uncomfortable or unsafe traveling to a location on GitLab's behalf due to concerns about the location, region, personal health, or other safety or security risks, please contact the People Safety & Security (PSS) team via HelpLab or email. The PSS team will help connect the team member with the right resources.

**Team member travel is not required unless deemed essential to the role. Please speak to your manager about whether the travel is mandatory and required for your role.**

## Trade Compliance Considerations

Although GitLab is an all-remote company that encourages working from anywhere, some places are subject to trade control restrictions. Team members **cannot** take company-owned devices to or otherwise work from US-embargoed countries or regions under any circumstances.

- **US-embargoed countries:** Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria
- **US-embargoed regions:** Crimea, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions of Ukraine
- **Additional restrictions:** Team members cannot take company-owned devices to or work from Russia or Belarus

This list is subject to change without notice.

## Business Travel Emergency Support and Insurance

### Quick Emergency Contacts

- **International SOS 24/7 Assistance:** +1 215 942 8226
- **Email:** philadelphia@internationalsos.com
- **Mobile App:** ISOS Assistance App (download and register with your GitLab email, using a unique password)

### Emergency Assistance Program with International SOS

GitLab provides team members with comprehensive emergency support through International SOS (ISOS) during business travel worldwide. Your coverage is automatic and year-round.

**When to use International SOS:**
- Medical emergencies or illness during travel (including payment of emergency medical expenses)
- Claims assistance for the Business Travel Insurance Policy
- Safety and security concerns
- Pre-trip planning and health advice

**How to access ISOS services:**
1. Download the ISOS Assistance App
2. Register using your GitLab email address (unique password, not your GitLab credentials)
3. Press "Need Assistance" to connect to the nearest emergency center

You can also access a digital membership card at `https://myportal.internationalsos.com/WebPortal/MyOrganisation`.

### Business Travel Insurance Coverage

GitLab's Business Travel Accident Policy (underwritten by AIG) provides comprehensive protection for team members traveling domestically and internationally on business.

| Coverage Type | Benefits |
|---|---|
| Accidental Death | 5× Annual Salary (up to USD 500,000) |
| Emergency Medical | Up to $250,000 per occurrence |
| Security Evacuation | Includes natural disaster evacuation |
| Personal Deviation | Extended coverage for personal travel (25% of business trip length) |
| Trip Duration | Covered for trips less than 180 days |
| Baggage Protection | Maximum of $2,500 |
| Family Coverage | Includes spouse, domestic partners, and children under 26 when traveling with you |

This policy is primary and will pay before any personal accident policies.

### Using the Policy

**If you need medical assistance while traveling:**
1. Contact International SOS immediately (app, phone, or email)
2. ISOS will arrange appropriate medical care
3. ISOS handles payments directly with providers
4. ISOS submits insurance claims to AIG on your behalf

**If you've already paid for medical care during business travel:** Follow the claims guide to submit your claim. ISOS can help with claim instructions.

### Visa Letter Documentation

For team members needing confirmation of coverage for visa applications, complete the AIG Visa Letter Form and follow the submission instructions on the form.

## Secure Your Data During Travels

- **VPN:** Use a VPN connection when on untrusted networks to avoid Man-in-the-Middle attacks.
- **Devices in public places:** Use a privacy screen filter to prevent shoulder-surfing.
- **Speaking in crowded places:** Ensure that conversations about restricted data happen in secure locations.
- **1Password Travel Mode:** Use Travel Mode before entering risky countries or leaving devices unattended to ensure vaults will be safe if a device is compromised.

### If customs or border agents demand a password

If customs, border control, or law enforcement agents demand the password to a laptop or mobile device (company-owned): GitLab recommends you comply without protesting. After complying, follow the process to engage **Security on-call** as soon as you can safely do so. Even if you did not provide a password, if any device is permanently seized or temporarily removed from sight, engage Security on-call.

### Airport security checkpoint guidance

- **Completely power-off** laptops and mobile devices before any security checkpoints. This reduces attacks that target sleep-mode machines where disk encryption is not being enforced.
- Prior to the trip, remove any sensitive data from your local machine that is not absolutely required.
- For high-risk travel (e.g. conferences like Defcon), request advice in the `#security-division` Slack channel.

## Expenses While Traveling

Understand the Global Travel and Expense Policy (`/handbook/finance/expenses/`) before you travel. Detailed expense-limit policy content is in the internal handbook at `https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/expenses/`.

title: GitLab Inc (US) Benefits Overview
content:
# GitLab Inc (US) Benefits Overview

**Source:** https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/inc-benefits-us/
**Fetched:** 2026-04-18

## Getting Started with Your Benefits

- **You have 30 days from your start date** to sign up for benefits through **PlanSource** (GitLab's benefits system).
- If you don't choose a plan within 30 days, you'll automatically get the **Medical Waiver Allowance** and won't have other optional coverage.

### Who Can Get Benefits?

You're eligible if you're a full-time GitLab team member working **at least 30 hours per week**. Benefits start on your first day.

You can also cover:
- Spouse or domestic partner
- Children up to age **26** (including adopted and stepchildren)
- Adult children with disabilities who can't support themselves

If you and an eligible family member both work at GitLab, you can only be covered once under the plans. Domestic partner coverage may be taxable income.

### How to Enroll

1. Login to **Workday** (`https://www.myworkday.com/gitlab/d/home.htmld`)
2. Click **View All Apps** → **Personal Information** app
3. Scroll to **External Links** → select **US Benefits Enrollment - PlanSource**

### Qualifying Life Events (change outside open enrollment)

- Marriage or divorce
- Birth or adoption of a child
- Spouse's employment changes
- Moving to a different state

**Log into PlanSource within 30 days** of the qualifying event and submit changes with required documentation.

## Medical Coverage

GitLab provides medical insurance through **Cigna** nationwide, with **Kaiser** options available for California and Hawaii residents. Opt out if you have coverage elsewhere.

### Medical Waiver Allowance

Already have group medical coverage? Opt out and receive a **$150 monthly benefit allowance** *(was $300 in 2025)* while still enrolling in dental, vision, and other benefits. You must actively waive medical coverage in PlanSource to receive this allowance.

### Cigna Medical Plans (three options)

1. **Cigna EPO** — Configured as PPO with limited out-of-network benefits ($10k/$20k deductible, $20k/$40k out-of-pocket max, 50% coinsurance out-of-network).
2. **Cigna HDHP (High Deductible Health Plan)** — Eligible for HSA contributions.
3. **Cigna PPO** — Standard PPO. Utah members get extended PPO network including Intermountain Healthcare System.

**GitLab HSA Contributions (HDHP enrollees):** $100/mo individual, $125/mo family. HSA contributions are taxable at the state level in California, Alabama, and New Jersey.

### Kaiser Medical Plans

Available in Hawaii and California. Kaiser claims window: **365 days** for out-of-network.

## Dental & Vision Coverage

- **Dental** through Cigna: DPPO Base Plan and DPPO Buy Up Plan.
- **Vision** through Cigna + EyeMed: Vision Base and Vision Buy Up.

## Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Through **New York Life Group Benefits** — no cost:
- **Behavioral Health:** 3 face-to-face sessions with counselors
- **Legal Services:** Free 30-minute consultations and 25% fee discounts
- **Financial Consultations:** Free 30-minute consultation and 25% tax services discount
- **Health Advocacy** and **Travel Protection** also included

## Life Insurance & AD&D

### Basic Life Insurance & AD&D (company-paid)

- **2× annual base salary** in Basic Life Insurance
- **Maximum benefit: $500,000**
- Equal AD&D coverage through Cigna / New York Life
- Automatic coverage from day one, no cost

### Supplemental Life Insurance

Additional voluntary coverage through Cigna. If you choose supplemental above the guaranteed amount, you (or dependent) may need to complete an Evidence of Insurability form.

Supplemental life insurance is **not** included in COBRA and ends on your last day.

## Disability Protection

- **Short-term and long-term disability insurance provided at no cost.**
- Replaces **up to 66.7% of base salary** for qualifying disabilities.
- Short-term disability benefit maximum period: **26 weeks**.
- Contact Absence Management at `leaves@gitlab.com` to apply.

**Claim process (NYLife):**
1. Submit Short-Term Disability application.
2. Within **3 business days**, NYLife contacts you for additional info if needed.
3. Decision.
4. Absence Management files all paperwork in Workday.

## 401(k) Plan with Company Match

- **Immediate eligibility and vesting.**
- **Company Match: 50% of contributions on the first 6% of earnings** (up to **$1,500 annually**).
- Investment options through **Fidelity NetBenefits**.
- Phone support: **Fidelity at 800-835-5097**.

### 401(k) Plan Features

- **After-tax contributions** with automatic Roth in-plan conversions available.
- **In-plan Roth conversion** (pre-tax source) — converted amounts taxable in year of conversion.
- **Rollovers** in or out via Fidelity forms.
- **401(k) Loans:** up to **50% of vested balance or $50,000**, whichever is less, at **Prime + 1% interest**.
- **401(k) Committee:** Chief People Officer, Principal Accounting Officer, Director of Total Rewards, Director Treasurer, Chief Legal Officer (observer).

## Flexible Spending & Health Savings Accounts

### Health Savings Account (HSA)

- GitLab monthly contribution: **$100 individual / $125 family**.
- Must be enrolled in the **HDHP** to be eligible.
- **Pre-tax** money for qualified medical expenses.
- Money rolls over annually and never expires.
- Invest balance in mutual funds, stocks, bonds once minimum balance is reached.
- At **age 65**, withdraw for any purpose without penalty (medical expenses remain tax-free).
- Transfer from a previous HSA: contact **WEX (Discovery)** at **866.451.3399** or `customerservice@discoverybenefits.com`.
- HSA stays with you forever after leaving GitLab (you become responsible for monthly admin fee).

## ID Cards & Access

- **Cigna:** Digital cards via myCigna website and mobile app.
- **Kaiser:** Physical cards mailed within **3 weeks**; digital cards via Kaiser online portal and mobile app.

## Medicare & Tax Documents

- GitLab plans are **Medicare-creditable**.
- Visit `medicare.gov` or call **1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227)**.
- **1095-C Form:** GitLab no longer automatically mails paper 1095-C forms (Paperwork Burden Reduction Act, Dec 2024). Access it via PlanSource → Documents → ACA Documents. Available no later than **March 2nd** of the following year.

## Summary of Key Numbers

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Benefits enrollment window | **30 days** from start date |
| Eligibility hours | **≥ 30 hours/week** |
| Dependent age limit | **26** |
| Medical Waiver Allowance | **$150 / month** |
| HSA contribution — single | **$100 / month** |
| HSA contribution — family | **$125 / month** |
| Basic Life Insurance | **2× base salary**, max **$500,000** |
| Disability replacement | **Up to 66.7% of base salary** |
| Short-term disability max period | **26 weeks** |
| 401(k) Match | **50% of first 6% of earnings**, up to **$1,500/year** |
| 401(k) loan limit | **50% of vested or $50,000** (lesser), Prime + 1% |
| Qualifying life event change window | **30 days** |

title: Do I need an RFP for an $18k software purchase?
content:
#people-ops-questions

Iona Grimaldi  3:12 PM
My team wants to buy a specialized design tool — annual cost is about $18k. Do I need to go through an RFP or is that below the threshold?

Alex (People Ops)  3:19 PM
Hi Iona — $18k/year is under the **$25k RFP threshold**, so **no competitive bids are required**. You just submit a Zip request through Okta for a new purchase request and Procurement will route it through the standard reviews (Security, Privacy, Legal, FP&A). Timeline is usually 5 days to 3 weeks depending on whether the vendor is new and how responsive their counsel is.

Iona Grimaldi  3:21 PM
Great — and if we wanted to expand to $30k next year?

Alex (People Ops)  3:24 PM
At $25k–$100k you'd need a **business-led quick-bid with 2 vendor bids**. $100k–$250k is 2–3 bids business-led. Over $250k is Procurement-led with 5+ bids. Exact table is in the procurement handbook page.
